title: The sharp matroid secretary conjecture
decision_reason: Explicit sharp utility conjecture, independent specialist corroboration, current theorem-scope comparisons, duplicate screening and separated A42 self-review passed.

problem_fingerprint.objects: Every finite matroid M=(E,I), with empty-set, heredity and augmentation axioms; arbitrary nonnegative weights w:E->R fixed before arrivals.
problem_fingerprint.model: Ground set and matroid known beforehand. Uniformly random permutation independent of fixed weights. Upon each labeled arrival its numerical weight is revealed; immediate irrevocable acceptance/rejection, and accepted set always independent. Randomized policies allowed, no information about unseen weights.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every finite M there exists an online policy A_M, chosen independently of w, that works for every nonnegative w.
problem_fingerprint.observable: Expected total accepted weight, over the random permutation and the policy's random coins; offline optimum max_{I in I} sum_{x in I} w(x).
problem_fingerprint.conclusion: Expected accepted weight at least OPT(M,w)/e, where e is Euler's number.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Explicit inequality fixes opposite competitive-ratio conventions. Rank-zero and all-zero-weight instances are vacuous. Known matroid allowed; no polynomial-time or per-optimum-element requirement imposed.
problem_fingerprint.scope: General matroids, numerical information on arrived weights, exact expected-utility guarantee. Not restricted to linear matroids, random assignment, prophet samples, future-weight queries, ordinal-only policies or mere existence of some constant factor.

independent_corroboration.assessment: STV21 explicitly distinguishes the usual utility conjecture from stronger performance measures. Singla independently retains the sharp factor e after a claimed general factor 4. Both author lists are disjoint from BHK+25.
independent_corroboration.currency: Checked against September 2026 primary statements and versions, including BDLSV26 found during the second pass.
independent_corroboration.limitation: Scholarly corroboration is distinct from independent review of this draft; the latter has not occurred.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Graphic matroids, including improved constants and a high-girth asymptotic guarantee.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: A restricted class and an asymptotic ratio do not prove the exact universal inequality.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Utility, ordinal, intersection and per-element probability guarantees are distinguished.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The draft asks only for numerical-value expected utility. Neither a restricted ordinal obstruction nor a stronger conjecture may replace it.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: General matroids; per-optimum-element probability at least 1/4. Suggested further improvement is explicitly unverified.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: This would settle the weak constant-factor conjecture, which is not admitted. It does not imply 1/e; §4 retains that target.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Announced single-sample prophet and matroid-intersection extensions.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Additional value samples and different feasibility systems do not strengthen the ordinary secretary guarantee to 1/e.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Exact 1/e guarantee for linear matroids via potentially expensive finite computation; general guarantee 1/64.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Linear representability is not automatic, while 1/64 falls short. The draft imposes no efficiency requirement, so runtime is not used to dismiss the linear result.
Independent value distributions and samples change the information model; no ordinary-secretary implication was found.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: A graphic-matroid rank-truncation counterexample, with ratios near 0.53.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: Refutes monotonicity under truncation, not the conjectured 1/e lower bound. The full relevant proof was inspected.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Specified greedy strategies and randomized partition strategies; the latter statement concerns probability competitiveness.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The quantified algorithm classes and performance criteria differ from unrestricted numerical utility policies.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: A 1/e or 1/2 guarantee using complete ordinal queries about unobserved elements.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The extra oracle exposes information unavailable in the candidate model.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: Linear matroids and known matroids admitting finitary modular extensions.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: The concluding discussion expressly excludes some matroids, including Vámos. This broader structural class is still not universal; the extension proof was read before admission.

resolution_scope_comparisons.result_scope: No strong forbidden-set construction of size one for all graphic matroids.
resolution_scope_comparisons.assessment: A restriction on an algorithmic framework does not rule out all admissible online policies.
